title: Torr and Pascal: The Vacuum Technology Ladder
h1: Torr and pascal — reading vacuum-system datasheets
description: Vacuum-chamber datasheets span 12 orders of magnitude of pressure. Here is the low-pressure ladder from rough to ultra-high vacuum in torr, mbar and Pa.

author.name: The Turbo Unit Converter engineering desk

hero: 1 torr = 133 Pa. Vacuum spans 15 decades from atmospheric down to 10⁻¹² torr — and each decade needs a different pump technology.
body: Vacuum technology cannot get away with one pump or one gauge. Every ten-fold drop in pressure needs a different technology, and every industry that uses vacuum has picked its favourite unit. Torr survives in the US; mbar dominates Europe; Pa is the SI answer nobody uses in vacuum labs.

> 1 torr = 133.3224 Pa = 1.333 mbar
> 1 mbar = 100 Pa = 0.7501 torr
> 1 Pa = 0.0075 torr = 0.01 mbar
> Atmospheric: 760 torr = 1013 mbar = 101,325 Pa

Rough vacuum: 760 – 1 torr (10³ – 1 mbar). Rotary vane pumps.
Medium vacuum: 1 – 10⁻³ torr (1 – 10⁻³ mbar). Roots blowers.
High vacuum: 10⁻³ – 10⁻⁸ torr (10⁻³ – 10⁻⁸ mbar). Turbomolecular pumps.
Ultra-high vacuum (UHV): 10⁻⁸ – 10⁻¹² torr. Ion pumps, cryopumps, sublimation pumps.
Extreme high vacuum (XHV): below 10⁻¹² torr. Combined pumping, extensive baking.

At 10⁻⁶ torr, the mean free path of a gas molecule is about 50 m — molecules travel between chamber walls without colliding with each other. At 10⁻¹⁰ torr (UHV), it takes over an hour for a monolayer of gas to deposit on a clean surface. Surface science and semiconductor deposition need this regime; ordinary vacuum coating does not.

US semiconductor fabs: torr. European semiconductor fabs: mbar. Physics research: increasingly Pa but torr and mbar dominate historical literature. Space environment: Pa (agreeing with ISO). No unification pressure in sight — the labels on gauges match the local convention.
## Worked example — CVD reactor at 10⁻³ torr

10⁻³ torr = 133 × 10⁻³ Pa = 0.133 Pa = 10⁻³ mbar. At 300 K this is a molecular density of 3.2 × 10¹³ molecules/cm³. A 10 sccm nitrogen inlet (standard cubic cm/min at 1 atm) is 4.5 × 10¹⁷ molecules/s — the reactor pumps this steadily to maintain the mTorr set point. Gas flow, pumping speed and chamber volume set the equilibrium pressure directly.
1 torr = 133 Pa = 1.33 mbar. Each decade of vacuum needs a different pump. Torr in US, mbar in EU, Pa in SI-strict labs.

faqs.q: Is torr the same as mmHg?
faqs.a: To six significant figures, yes. Modern SI-strict practice prefers 'torr' because mmHg depends on mercury density and gravity, while torr is a defined ratio (1/760 atm).
1 micron = 1 millitorr = 0.133 Pa. HVAC vacuum service quotes down to 500 microns for AC line dehydration.

faqs.q: Why can't a rotary pump reach UHV?
faqs.a: Backstreaming oil vapour sets a floor around 10⁻³ torr. UHV requires oil-free pumps (turbo, ion, cryo) and bakeout to drive off adsorbed water.
